paragraphs: In Grimsby, Cleethorpes, Immingham and the villages around them, children in care are looked after by North East Lincolnshire Council's own fostering service, based at New Oxford House in Grimsby, and by the independent agencies shown above. The council says it wants children in care to stay close to the communities they know, which is why it looks for carers who live locally.

The council's fostering statement of purpose for 2025-26 records that on 1 July 2025 it had 84 approved mainstream fostering households caring for 131 children, and 52 kinship households, where a relative or family friend fosters, caring for 48 children. It approved six new households in the previous year. The council offers long-term care, short stays from one night to a few weeks, short breaks for disabled children and kinship care, and its fostering panel meets every fortnight.

The council describes weekly and annual allowances for each child, with more for holidays and experience; its statement says the weekly allowance follows the national minimum allowances and that carers also receive a skills payment at one of three levels. It also mentions up to a full council tax discount for its carers, round-the-clock support, Fostering Network membership and a fostering buddy. Its initial requirements are being over 21, having a spare room and having the right to live and work in the UK.
Whether you choose the council or an agency, ask each one what training, out-of-hours help and payments it offers for the kind of fostering you have in mind.
